source: Bavli Nazir 23a / Horayot 10b; Bereshit Rabbah 51 (via Minchat Shai on 19:33)
claim_en: THE THIRD DOTTED PLACE: ובקומה ('and when she ROSE' — the elder daughter, 19:33) — the schools expound the dot: 'in her lying he knew not, but in her RISING he knew.' SNAPSHOT carries the dot in the stream (encoded at the qof-position where the tradition names the vav — attachment noted). Third of the ten reached, third present.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 19:33 (the Ramah: 'the first plene, the last defective')
claim_en: ...and the dot has a SPELLING partner: the two risings of Lot's daughters — the FIRST (19:33) written PLENE with vav, the SECOND (19:35) DEFECTIVE (probed: no vav, no dot). The dotted vav exists only in the elder's rising — the letter the derash hangs on is the letter only that verse has.

source: Masekhet Soferim 4 (no dispute); Bavli Shevuot 35b; Rambam's codification (via Minchat Shai on 19:18)
claim_en: THE ONE HOLY NAME OF LOT — the mirror of Abraham's one profane: 'all the Names said of Lot are PROFANE except this one, HOLY: אל נא אדני ... to KEEP MY SOUL ALIVE — He who has power to kill and to make alive' (19:18). SNAPSHOT: the nun in qamatz, the sacred-form pointing; the layer's fourth station, this time undisputed and codified.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 19:16 (the Mikhlol; the Masorah's seven)
claim_en: THE CHAIN OF HESITATION: ויתמהמה ('and he LINGERED') carries the SHALSHELET (the chain accent — Scripture's rarest, 'seven in the Masorah, quavering and pausing'), and its final mem takes QAMATZ because the chain has a pause's force. SNAPSHOT: the chain-sign in the stream — and the accent's whole-Torah census, probed direct, is EXACTLY FOUR: Lot's lingering (19:16), the servant's prayer (24:12), Joseph's refusal (39:8), the ordination slaughter (Lev 8:23); the Masorah's other three live in the Writings (edges).

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 19:23 (the sevirin Masorah)
claim_en: A SEVIRIN ('presumed') READING — a new Masorah class for the audit: השמש יצא ('the sun WENT OUT' — masculine verb on the usually-feminine sun): one of THREE places Scripture writes יצא where יצאה is presumed — one in the Torah (here), one in the Prophets, one in the Writings. SNAPSHOT: the masculine form stands.
THE HE-TO-HE VERSE, opening: the sunrise verse BEGINS with he (השמש) — the Kitzur: the verse runs he-to-he, 'five mils he walked before the sun came out' (the letter-value of he = 5).
THE HE-TO-HE VERSE, closing: ...and ENDS with he (צערה, 'toward Zoar' — with the directional he). The five-mil escort reading rides the two letters (named).

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 19:25 and 19:8 (the Masorah of parashat Toledot)
claim_en: THE EIGHT SHORT THESE: האל ('these' — the demonstrative written without its final he) — the Masorah: EIGHT in the language where האלה is presumed. SNAPSHOT, lemma-locked: exactly eight — TWO in this chapter (the daughters offered 'to THESE men,' 19:8; 'He overthrew THESE cities,' 19:25), Isaac's covenant pair (26:3/4), the abominations (Lev 18:27), and Deuteronomy's three. The overthrow rides a shortened word.

קומו צאו ('RISE, GO OUT of this place') — the pair exactly TWICE in the Torah: Lot's sons-in-law at midnight (19:14) and PHARAOH at midnight ('rise, go out from among my people,' Exod 12:31): Sodom's exit-formula is the Exodus' exit-formula — the Kitzur reads the mockers who stayed against those who died in the darkness (named).

כדרך ('after the MANNER of...') — exactly TWICE in the Torah: 'the manner of all the earth' (the daughters' plan, 19:31) and 'a day's JOURNEY' of quail (Num 11:31) — the Kitzur: 'as here bed-manner, so there — they craved illicitly in asking the quail.'

ונחיה ('that we may KEEP ALIVE seed') — the intensive-stem form exactly TWICE in the Torah, both in the cave (19:32, 19:34); the Masorah's third: 'that we may keep the HORSES AND MULES alive' (Ahab's famine, I Kings 18:5; edge) — 'they did a beast's deed' (Kitzur). Morph-locked census (the brothers' 'we shall live' rides the simple stem).

THE SLEEP IN THE FINALS: הצעירה הן שכבתי אמש ('...to the younger: behold, I lay last night') — the final letters, read backward, spell שינה ('SLEEP'): 'he was asleep and felt nothing' (the ordered string הניש verified; the reversal named).

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 19:20 (the Masorah's mnemonic: 'Lot below, David above')
claim_en: אמלטה נא ('let me ESCAPE, please') — read MIL'RA (stress forward) with DAGESH in the nun of the plea-word; its Scripture-twin (I Sam 20:29, David's escape-plea) reads mil'el — the Masorah's mnemonic: 'Lot below, David above.' SNAPSHOT: the doubled nun exact (the Samuel leg rides as an edge).

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 19:22 (the Ramah: 'none like it in the Torah')
claim_en: עד באך ('until your COMING there') — defective (no vav) with the bare kaf: the Ramah marks it UNIQUE in the Torah, and Minchat Shai wonders aloud why the Masorah's Noach-list omits it. SNAPSHOT: one token, exactly as described.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 19:30 (the Hilleli; the Ramah's three-plene rule)
claim_en: THE ZOAR SPELLING LAW, full side: 'צוער three plene in this class' (the Ramah) — and the naming verse itself is the mnemonic ('therefore the city's name was called ZOAR,' 19:22). SNAPSHOT: plene at the naming.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 19:30 (the same rule's lean side)
claim_en: THE ZOAR SPELLING LAW, lean side: the VERY NEXT VERSE writes the city defective (צערה, 'toward Zoar,' 19:23) — as do the war-annal's tokens (13:10, 14:2, 14:8) and Moses' vista (Deut 34:3): the city is full only at its naming and Lot's ascent (19:30's two, probed). One verse apart, the law turns.

כקיטר ('like the SMOKE of the kiln') — the Ramah: both smoke-words of the verse (the land's קיטר and the kiln's כקיטר) plene-yod, lean-vav. SNAPSHOT: both, in the one verse where Abraham looks down on the overthrow.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 19:31 (our books and the Masorah — against the Hilleli)
claim_en: לבוא ('to COME in to us') — the Hilleli copy reads defective; all our books and the Masorah's own nine-defective list (which omits this one) rule PLENE. SNAPSHOT: plene — the run's first arbitration AGAINST the Hilleli.
